name: Bharti Airtel Ltd
title: Bharti Airtel Ltd - 532454 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

read.thesis: Airtel's Q1 call shows ARPU-led growth with supply discipline in radio capex, but FWA was pulled back on acquisition quality and B2B growth is capex-heavy; the 4-5% ARPU architecture view is restated as a multi-year wish, not guidance.

summary.headline: Airtel group revenue Rs.58,500 Cr (+5.7% QoQ), EBITDAaL Rs.29,800 Cr at 51% margin; India mobile ARPU Rs.264 and record 1 million postpaid adds.
summary.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 (quarter ended June 30, 2026) as another strong quarter, with consolidated revenue of Rs.58,500 Cr and EBITDAaL of Rs.29,800 Cr (up 4.2%). Capex was about Rs.13,390 Cr, leaving operating free cash flow above Rs.16,450 Cr. India mobile added 3.3 million revenue-earning customers and a record 1 million postpaid customers, but home broadband net adds slowed to 473,000 as the company tightened acquisition quality and pivoted toward fiber over FWA. Management also flagged rising memory and chipset costs hurting FWA economics, and reiterated plans for Airtel Money's London listing in 2H 2026, Nxtra data center scale-up toward 1 GW, and Indus expansion into three African markets.

segments.name: Africa
segments.commentary: Constant-currency revenue growth of 5.7%; annualised EBITDA above Rs.35,000 Cr; over last five years constant-currency revenue CAGR above 20% and EBITDA CAGR above 24%. Airtel Money Q1 revenue above $400 Mn, up 26% YoY constant currency. Airtel stake raised to over 79% via EPS-accretive share swap.

segments.name: India excluding passive infra
segments.commentary: Growth of 3.6% QoQ as stated; net debt excluding passive infra now below 1x EBITDAaL. Mobile added 3.3 Mn revenue-earning customers and 5 Mn smartphone data customers; postpaid now 8%+ of base.

segments.name: Homes (India)
segments.commentary: Net adds of 473,000, a moderation from prior quarters, attributed to tighter acquisition quality after aggressive low-price FWA offers. Digital TV added 6,000 customers led by IPTV.

segments.name: Bharti Hexacom
segments.commentary: Mobile customer base 29 Mn, net adds about 210,000, smartphone adds 344,000; homes net adds 75,000 with revenue growth about 8% QoQ (homes, office and other).

segments.name: Data centers (Nxtra)
segments.commentary: Market share about 12%; ambition of 1 GW from current 120-130 MW. Google contract included. Nxtra raised $1 Bn externally; management says Nxtra will need further debt funding.

segments.name: Airtel Cloud
segments.commentary: 33 customers after adding 11 this quarter; MeitY certifications received. Management says the business needs talent, capital, go-to-market and solutions.

segments.name: Financial services (Airtel Finance / NBFC)
segments.commentary: Lending went live about nine months after licence application; monthly loan disbursements above Rs.750 Cr via Airtel Finance. Payments bank monthly transacting users about 120 Mn.

guidance_outlook: Management expects mid-term mobile ARPU headroom from upgrades, unlimited-plan migration, postpaid acceleration and Fast Lane; long-term ARPU growth of 4-5% (or slightly higher) assumed over 5-7 years once tariff architecture is repaired.

Home broadband: fiber is the priority; FWA restricted to locations without fiber access; acquisition quality improvement expected to unwind in coming quarters (per Bharti Hexacom commentary, next two quarters).
Data centers: target of 1 GW in the next few years; about 200 MW upcoming build over next couple of years plus Mumbai land parcels being finalised.
Airtel Business: digital services expected to accelerate; overall Airtel Business EBITDA margin expected to trend slightly downward over time as digital mix rises, with revenue growth emphasised.
Airtel Money planned London listing in second half of 2026.
Management said it will not hold back capex where needed; capex in the near term to step up for data centers; radio capex has moderated and 5G standalone capex is modest.
Indus Towers expansion into Africa starts with three markets; further countries are not yet committed.
capex_capacity: Quarterly capex about Rs.13,390 Cr; the company says radio capex has moderated over the last couple of years, with most spend on transport and fiber (including homes).
Data centers: rapid build-out expected, lumpy as land is acquired; 120-130 MW today heading to 1 GW.
Cloud: first-round investment completed across three regions; further capacity added as it fills, modular.
Over the last three years about 139,000 km of fiber deployed.
Bharti Hexacom capex directed to 5G densification, network modernisation, fiberisation and homes/IPTV.
demand_pricing: India mobile ARPU Rs.264, helped by one extra day; drivers cited as data-led upgrades, unlimited plan migration, postpaid acceleration via Fast Lane (5G network slicing).
Management says industry pricing architecture must change to charge for data; no tariff hike assumed in near term.
Wholesale B2B business is low-margin and under price pressure; messaging shifting from SMS to WhatsApp. Connectivity market grows at low single digits.
FWA acquisition was hurt by very aggressive low entry pricing, causing round-tripping and churn; memory and chipset prices raised FWA unit economics costs.
Refurbished phones circulating are rising with inflation, supporting data sub-additions; management sees no impact yet.
International roaming improving QoQ after West Asia-related decline in prior quarter.
Bharti Hexacom: Rajasthan described as very competitive; Northeast position comfortable.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the strong mobile ARPU improvement QoQ and is it sustainable without a tariff hike?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited headroom from data-led upgrades, unlimited plan migration and postpaid acceleration with Fast Lane; sees mid-term headroom, with long-term growth requiring pricing architecture repair.

qa_highlights.question: How is Airtel Business growth split across connectivity, cloud and data center, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Business has three parts: connectivity, low-margin wholesale and digital (data center, cloud, CPaaS, IoT, cybersecurity). Digital is accelerating; a step-up in global connectivity deals boosted the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Will capex shift toward AI infrastructure and what is the capex envelope (about $4 Bn)?
qa_highlights.answer: Radio capex moderated; large spend on transport and fiber. 5G standalone is mostly software and modest. Data center build will drive rapid capex step-up; company will not hold back on needed capex.

qa_highlights.question: Will Nxtra funding come from external sponsorship or the parent balance sheet?
qa_highlights.answer: Undecided; Nxtra will need equity and debt, and the choice between parent balance sheet and external funding will be taken over time.

qa_highlights.question: How much customer improvement does Fast Lane deliver and does FWA churn change the growth run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Fast Lane gives better experience mainly in congested networks; overall network efficiency lifts speeds for all. FWA aggressive pricing was pulled back; no FWA market-share target, only home broadband target. Churn figure not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 1 GW data center ambition supported by demand and land?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes: contracts including Google are in place, a few hundred MW build is underway, and Mumbai land parcels being finalised to fill the gap.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Hexacom mobile net adds weaken and was there a change in home broadband targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to seasonality with more additions in 2H; home broadband slowdown reflects a deliberate acquisition-quality correction, with no change to market size or share assumptions.

qa_highlights.question: What drove lower energy costs at Hexacom and depreciation jump?
qa_highlights.answer: Solar-powered sites benefited from seasonality and one-offs; underlying trend in line. Depreciation rise due to one extra day and IPTV rollout.

risks_watch: FWA/homes net adds slowed to 473,000 in Airtel India and about 75,000 in Hexacom; management expects unwinding of acquisition correction in coming quarters.
Rising memory and chipset prices pressuring FWA economics and potentially smartphone affordability.
Diesel price increases; only partial impact seen in the quarter, with stocks in DG sets; cost headwinds acknowledged.
Data center capex is lumpy and will need external or parent funding (Nxtra debt).
Airtel Business margin may trend slightly down as digital mix rises; cloud conversion cycles are long (per management, sovereign and large deals are the main wins).
Airtel Finance: potential perceived conflict with partner NBFCs; management says compliance with RBI LSP rules.
Industry pricing architecture unresolved; ARPU growth dependent on tariff repair not in management control.

key_quotes: We delivered yet another quarter of strong performance across the group.
The fact is that Nxtra will need funding and that funding will be obviously there is some equity infusion, but there will also be a debt that will be raised at Nxtra.

I think my message would be that wherever we think that there is a legitimate need for the business in order to step up growth, in order to be competitive or to actually plan some of these newer bets ; as a Company, we will not hold back on capex.
It is just a bit of change in the go to market because of the quality of acquisition.
As soon as we can correct this architecture, it’ll be great, but it needs, like, we cannot do it single handedly.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the group's growth, Africa, data centers and Airtel Money, but cautious on homes/FWA, where management acknowledged a deliberate acquisition-quality correction and pulled back aggressive pricing. Evasive on return-on-capital targets, Nxtra funding source, and the timing of tariff repair, which management said it cannot drive alone.

growth.why: Management guides long-term industry ARPU growth of 4-5% (maybe slightly higher) over 5-7 years and a Nxtra path to 1 GW with ~200 MW upcoming, but no company-level revenue growth number is given and the data-centre build is only partly specified by timing.
